title: GST 114 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER 13 ( THE PARAGRAPH AS A UNIT OF AN ESSAY )
subject: GST 114

questions.question: A paragraph is described as which of the following in an essay?
questions.explanation: The paragraph is a mechanical device in an essay.

questions.question: An essay can lose its effectiveness if its paragraphs are poorly what?
questions.explanation: An essay can lose effectiveness if its paragraphs are poorly structured.

questions.question: A paragraph plays the same role as which element in a book?
questions.explanation: A paragraph plays the same role as a chapter heading in a book.

questions.question: A paragraph is a group of sentences organized around which element?
questions.explanation: A paragraph revolves around a particular idea in an essay.

questions.question: The central function of a paragraph is to supply information to the reader in what form?
questions.explanation: A paragraph supplies information to the reader by installments.

questions.question: Which type of paragraph has no indentation but uses spaces between lines?
questions.explanation: A block paragraph has no indentation and uses spaces between lines.

questions.question: Every paragraph must fulfill which condition?
questions.explanation: Every paragraph must be related to the thesis statement of the essay.

questions.question: The physical sign of a traditional paragraph is called what?
questions.explanation: The traditional physical sign of a paragraph is indentation.

questions.question: The length of a paragraph depends on which factor?
questions.explanation: The length depends on whether the topic is expository, argumentative, or narrative.

questions.question: A typical paragraph in an essay consists of about how many sentences?
questions.explanation: A typical paragraph consists of about six sentences.

questions.question: A paragraph should not be excessively what?
questions.explanation: A paragraph should not be too excessively long.

questions.question: Which are the essential elements of a paragraph?
questions.explanation: Essential elements are topic sentence, supporting sentences, concluding sentence.

questions.question: The structure of a paragraph has how many major parts?
questions.explanation: A paragraph has three major parts: topic sentence, supporting sentences, concluding sentence.

questions.question: The topic sentence reveals which part of a paragraph?
questions.explanation: The topic sentence reveals the main idea of a paragraph.

questions.question: A topic sentence is most frequently found in which position?
questions.explanation: The topic sentence is most frequently found at the beginning of a paragraph.

questions.question: The topic sentence may be a statement, generalization, or what?
questions.explanation: A topic sentence may be a statement, generalization, or question.

questions.question: Which sentence directly explains the topic sentence?
questions.explanation: A major supporting sentence directly explains the main idea.

questions.question: Supporting sentences may include which of the following?
questions.explanation: Supporting sentences may include facts, quotes, and examples.

questions.question: A minor supporting sentence helps which sentence develop?
questions.explanation: A minor supporting sentence helps the major supporting sentence develop.

questions.question: Which sentence ends a well-written paragraph?
questions.explanation: A well-written paragraph ends with a good concluding sentence.

questions.question: The concluding sentence may give a summary of what?
questions.explanation: The concluding sentence may give a summary of the main topic.

questions.question: Narration as a method of paragraph development involves what?
questions.explanation: Narration involves telling a story.

questions.question: Description as a method of paragraph development uses words to do what?
questions.explanation: Description paints something or someone by use of words.

questions.question: Comparison as a method shows how two subjects are what?
questions.explanation: Comparison shows how two subjects are similar.

questions.question: Contrast as a method points out how two subjects are what?
questions.explanation: Contrast points out how two subjects are different.

questions.question: Example as a method provides what for an idea?
questions.explanation: Example provides illustrations of an idea or topic.

questions.question: Classification organizes things that share what?
questions.explanation: Classification groups things with the same qualities.

questions.question: Division takes out a part from the whole to do what?
questions.explanation: Division takes out a part to fully discuss it.

questions.question: Definition as a method gives the meaning of what?
questions.explanation: Definition gives the meaning of a term, idea, or concept.

questions.question: Process analysis tells how something is what?
questions.explanation: Process analysis tells how something is achieved or done.

questions.question: Cause and effect shows what?
questions.explanation: Cause and effect shows reasons and results.

questions.question: Which quality means a paragraph has only one main idea?
questions.explanation: Unity is the principle of singleness of purpose.

questions.question: Which quality refers to logical arrangement of sentences?
questions.explanation: Coherence refers to the arrangement of sentences in a logical way.

questions.question: Correctness in a paragraph means it is written in what?
questions.explanation: Correctness means the paragraph is written in correct Standard English.

questions.question: Order in a paragraph refers to the arrangement of what?
questions.explanation: Order refers to the way supporting sentences are ordered.

questions.question: Completeness requires a paragraph to have what?
questions.explanation: A complete paragraph must have a topic sentence and supporting sentences.

questions.question: Which quality is achieved by using sentence connectors and pronouns?
questions.explanation: Coherence is achieved by using sentence connectors and pronouns.

questions.question: Paragraph transition marks a shift in what?
questions.explanation: Paragraph transition marks a shift in thought from one paragraph to the next.

questions.question: Transitions between paragraphs help the reader to do what?
questions.explanation: Transitions help the reader anticipate or comprehend new information.

questions.question: Which transition word shows exception or contrast?
questions.explanation: However is a transition word showing exception or contrast.

questions.question: Which transition word shows sequence or order?
questions.explanation: First is a transition word showing sequence or order.

questions.question: Which transition word shows emphasis?
questions.explanation: Indeed is a transition word showing emphasis.

questions.question: Which transition word shows time?
questions.explanation: Afterward is a transition word showing time.

questions.question: The first step in writing a good paragraph is what?
questions.explanation: The first step is to think before you write.

questions.question: A dictionary and thesaurus are used to do what?
questions.explanation: A dictionary and thesaurus are used to add words to express ideas.

questions.question: The concluding paragraph should restate what?
questions.explanation: The concluding paragraph should restate the primary arguments.

questions.question: A good conclusion should leave the reader with what?
questions.explanation: A good conclusion leaves the reader with something to think about.

questions.question: The concluding paragraph should be proofread before what?
questions.explanation: Proofread your essay before turning it in.

questions.question: A paragraph supplies ideas to the reader in what manner?
questions.explanation: Paragraphs supply ideas in manageable, regulated, and coherent instalments.

questions.question: Which element governs the main idea of a paragraph?
questions.explanation: The main idea of a paragraph is governed by the topic sentence.
